beats.say: A penny signs you up for a music library. The bill follows later.
Then you must buy a minimum number of albums at regular prices.
If you miss the deadline, the next selection ships automatically.
Revenue peaked at $1.4 billion in 1996, fell to $17 million in 2014. Odd.
But it does a job: a negative-option trap.
The auto-ship clause forces a purchase unless you opt out.
Most members never opt out, so the club keeps billing.
That flow kept revenue high until a 2015 bankruptcy filing.
A coffee club gives a free mug for $1, then $15 monthly unless you cancel.
A tiny upfront cost can hide a big bill. Follow for more.
